sources.title: Fleisher and colleagues, When Did the Swahili Become Maritime? (2015)
sources.note: Original paper read through indexed PMC and publisher text; direct PMC access challenged. Background and navigation sections establish African coastal settlement, multiple centres and documented routes. Its stronger claim that maritime identity began after 1000 is debated, and is not presented here as settled fact.

sources.title: UNESCO: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara
sources.note: Direct official statement of outstanding universal value. Building dates approximate; Portuguese fort and decline dated only to the sixteenth century here.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum, Kilwa copper coin HCR20159
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue gives Arabic transcription, translation, authority, mint, measurements and approximate date. Arabic joins the three reverse lines with spaces; no independently deciphered coin photograph is claimed.

sources.title: Quintana Morales and colleagues, Diet, economy, and culinary practices at the height of precolonial Swahili urbanism (2022)
sources.note: Direct original article extraction. Three passages use botanical finds, multi-proxy dietary analysis and daub-house archaeology. The seven individuals are a limited sample, not all coastal residents.

sources.title: Stephanie Wynne-Jones, The public life of the Swahili stonehouse, 14th to 15th centuries AD (2013)
sources.note: Original article read directly earlier and corroborated in indexed repository and author-uploaded full text. House 44 spindle whorls and room SM010 are specific excavated contexts.

sources.title: CONCH project and Songo Mnara community: site interpretation brochure
sources.note: Direct two-page project brochure acknowledges Tanzanian Antiquities Division and Village Ruins Committee. Historical lamps, beams and benches distinguished from modern visitor toilets. Its interpretation of the Palace house as a merchant residence is more precise than the older monument label.

sources.title: UNESCO: Historic Town and Archaeological Site of Gedi
sources.note: Direct official statement. Inland location, walls and social stratification, trade including enslaved people, and tenth to seventeenth-century chronology.

sources.title: National Museums of Kenya: Gedi conservation management plan
sources.note: Direct official PDF, draft statement of outstanding universal value, printed pages 13 to 15 (human PDF pages 15 to 17). Cites surviving water and sanitation features without adopting sweeping world-first comparisons.

proposedOverrides.name: Swahili coastal city-states
proposedOverrides.summary: Connected East African coastal towns with distinct rulers, households and Indian Ocean trading links.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Indexed HB record spans 1000 to 1650. Decoded geometry follows East African coast from approximately 37.734 to 47.637 E and 11.230 S to 4.096 N, contracting northward after 1492. Identified as regional coastal aggregate, not a single state or all Islamic cities worldwide. Kilwa, Songo Mnara and Gedi are named examples; northern Somali ports have distinct local histories. No alias association with modern Zanzibar or Somalia records. No asserted common collapse at map endpoint.
